STATUS: BLOCKED 2026-10-13 on deno's own Cargo.lock. The release binary carries no
cargo-auditable data (no .dep-v0 section), so Trivy never saw its crates and the
published 2.9.7 passed the gate blind. The v2.9.7 Cargo.lock, scanned with the gate's
flags, holds 7 fixable findings, and the crate-version strings inside the binary
confirm all 7 ship:
  hickory-resolver 0.25.2  GHSA-5j98-2g5x-46v6 HIGH, GHSA-6f2x-v7q7-m7m5 MEDIUM  (fix 0.26.2)
  hickory-proto 0.25.2     GHSA-q2qq-hmj6-3wpp MEDIUM                            (fix 0.26.1)
  rustls 0.23.40           GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc MEDIUM                            (fix 0.23.45)
  rand 0.8.5, 0.9.2        GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc LOW                               (fix 0.8.6/0.9.3)
  xxhash-rust 0.8.15       GHSA-6g2r-675j-hx59 LOW                               (fix 0.8.16)
Not a VEX: only three are provably absent. cargo tree on v2.9.7 resolves hickory-resolver
to [default,serde,system-config,tokio] with no __dnssec feature, so hickory-resolver-0.25.2
src/resolver.rs:91-104 never builds the DnssecDnsHandle (GHSA-5j98); rand has no `log`
feature and xxhash-rust only `xxh64`. The CNAME and name-compression bugs (Deno.resolveDns,
ext/net/ops.rs:1187-1191) and the rustls one (every fetch and TLS connection) are
reachable in a general runtime.
Not a source build: hickory 0.25 to 0.26 is a breaking API change (deno PR #36322, open
and conflicting), so a cargo update cannot take it.
UNBLOCK when a deno release pins hickory-resolver >= 0.26.2, hickory-proto >= 0.26.1 and
rustls >= 0.23.45 (main still had 0.25.2 and 0.23.40 on 2026-10-13): add the version with
its zip and Cargo.lock sha256s, set BLOCKED=0, dispatch. The recipe installs that
Cargo.lock in the image, so the gate scans every crate; VEX what is left only with the
feature evidence above.
